mapping_rules.bit_source: BIT_SOURCE is kept in the primary wing fit because it covers essentially the whole annulus; it is the source mask, not a defect. A BIT_SOURCE-excluded variant is reported as a diagnostic. It is excluded only from the diagnostic sky background annulus (5-8 native px).
mapping_rules.cutout_cache: sha256(f'{access_url}|{ra:.8f}|{dec:.8f}|{size:.6f}').fits in each cutout cache dir, mirroring IrsaClient._cutout_cache_path (irsa_client.py:443-455).
mapping_rules.lvf_prediction: TAP p.poly is the full 2040x2040 detector footprint (hex EWKB). Vertex 0 -> detector (0,0), vertex 1 -> (2040,0), vertex 3 -> (0,2040); RA is wrapped to [-180,180). The target's detector X/Y is mapped through the cached WCS-WAVE lookup (sip=None). The prediction is validated against the 3 cached visits.
mapping_rules.psf_zone: Full-frame detector X/Y = cutout target pixel - CRPIX1A/CRPIX2A; 11x11 zones of 185.4545 detector px; zone index = zone_y*11 + zone_x. The PSF cube planes are normalized to 1.
mapping_rules.spectrum_channel_to_visit: The golden manifest band_stats[band].artifact_uris are the visits selected by _select_visits (up to 3, evenly spaced in MJD). Each visit contributes one channel; the per-visit wavelength is read from WCS-WAVE (key='W', sip=None). Channels are matched by epoch + detector + |Delta lambda| < 5e-4 um.
mapping_rules.wing_annulus: 1.2 <= r <= 4.2 native pixels, with r measured from the propagated target position to native pixel centers; native scale from the cutout WCS (~6.15 arcsec/px). P_i is the normalized local HDU 5 PSF fraction in native pixel i.

notes: All FITS access is by EXTNAME; the empty primary HDU data is never read.

Primary wing mask is PHOTOMETRY_EXCLUDE_MASK (hard + warning, including DICHROIC). BIT_SOURCE is kept because it covers most of these frames (e.g., ~93% of the Barnard's Star frame stats); a BIT_SOURCE-excluded variant is reported.
A failed wing gate never yields photometry; diagnostic fluxes are labelled diagnostic_only.
QR3 products expose EPSF (441x33x33, 5x oversampling) instead of the HDU 5 PSF cube; EPSF covers only +/-3.3 native px and cannot evaluate the 1.2-4.2 px gate.
TAP row counts are real IRSA queries; no epochs are fabricated or interpolated.
Telemetry sizes use real 240x240 single-band reprojections and a nearest-neighbor Table 16 flag plane.

barnards_star.verdict_reason: 0/54 channels pass the f_wing>=0.12 and N_wing>=8 gate. The clean wing fraction is 0.0012 (median) because the 1.2-4.2 native-px annulus is dominated by SUR_ERROR / TRANSIENT / OVERFLOW / BLOOM. Even with no flag masking, only 23/38 PSF-bearing channels pass and the median unmasked annulus fraction is 0.1379. HDU 5 PSF wing recovery cannot replace the current aperture photometry as specified.

The 2,483 TAP rows form one continuous 520-day season: there is no gap > 60 days, so the specified clustering yields 1 cluster, not 5-6 epochs. The NEP cadence is rolling band pairs (D3+D6, D2+D5, D1+D4), and D2/D5 have only 89 exposures each. At a 10-day gap there are 7 natural blocks and only 1 block has all six bands present, with D2/D5 partial. Five to six well-populated, complete 6-band epochs are not supported by the TAP data; do not interpolate them.

telemetry.verdict_reason: The <45 KB claim is not realistic for a real 240x240 float16 MJy/sr plane plus uint32 Table 16 flags. The float16 plane dominates and gzips poorly (~78-99 KB alone); both arrays gzip to ~80-103 KB. The uint32 flag plane is tiny (~1.5-4.5 KB gzipped). The honest sidecar budget is ~80-105 KB gzipped, or ~105-140 KB as base64 JSON.
